content: 1. Closely monitor patients for adverse effects related to the use of gilteritinib. Both gilteritinib and lopinavir are known to prolong the QTc interval. It is recommended to avoid their concomitant use or consider alternative medications. If coadministration is unavoidable, obtain ECGs at baseline, during concurrent use, and as clinically indicated. Discontinue therapy if the QTc interval exceeds 500 ms or if there is a change from baseline greater than 60 ms. 2. Lopinavir increases the levels or effects of glasdegib by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Both lopinavir and glasdegib prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. If coadministration is unavoidable, monitor for an increased risk of QTc prolongation. 3. Lopinavir increases the levels or effects of glecaprevir/pibrentasvir by reducing their metabolism. Avoid coadministration of glecaprevir/pibrentasvir with lopinavir, as lopinavir is a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor and P-glycoprotein substrate. 4. Both granisetron and lopinavir prolong the QTc interval. Avoid their concomitant use or consider alternative medications. 5. Lopinavir increases the levels or effects of haloperidol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 6. Histrelin increases the toxicity of lopinavir by prolonging the QTc interval, which raises the risk of torsades de pointes. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 7. Both hydroxychloroquine sulfate and lopinavir prolong the QTc interval. Avoid their concomitant use or consider alternative medications. 8. Lopinavir increases the levels or effects of hydroxyprogesterone caproate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 9. Both hydroxyzine and lopinavir prolong the QTc interval. Avoid their concomitant use or consider alternative medications. 10. Lopinavir increases the levels or effects of ibrutinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. If a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor must be used short-term (e.g., for anti-infectives lasting ≤7 days), interrupt ibrutinib therapy until the strong CYP3A4 inhibitor is discontinued. 11. Lopinavir increases the levels or effects of idelalisib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. If coadministered with strong CYP3A inhibitors, monitor for signs of idelalisib toxicity and follow dosage modification recommendations if adverse reactions occur. 12. Lopinavir increases the levels or effects of imatinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 13. Lopinavir increases the levels or effects of infigratinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 14. Both inotuzumab and lopinavir prolong the QTc interval. Avoid their concomitant use or consider alternative medications. If coadministration is unavoidable, obtain ECGs and electrolytes before and after initiating any QTc-prolonging drug, and monitor periodically as clinically indicated. 15. Both isoflurane and lopinavir prolong the QTc interval. Avoid their concomitant use or consider alternative medications. 16. Lopinavir increases the levels or effects of isradipine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 17. Lopinavir increases the levels or effects of itraconazole by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both itraconazole and lopinavir prolong the QTc interval. Avoid their concomitant use or consider alternative medications. 18. Lopinavir increases the levels or effects of ivosidenib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration of strong CYP3A4 inhibitors with ivosidenib or replace with alternative therapies. If coadministration is unavoidable, reduce the ivosidenib dose to 250 mg daily. After discontinuing the strong CYP3A4 inhibitor for at least 5 half-lives, increase the ivosidenib dose to the recommended 500 mg daily. Both ivosidenib and lopinavir prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration of QTc-prolonging drugs with ivosidenib or replace with alternative therapies. 19. Ivosidenib decreases the levels or effects of lopinavir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. If coadministration is unavoidable, monitor patients for loss of therapeutic effect of these drugs. 20. Lopinavir increases the levels or effects of ixabepilone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 21. Lopinavir increases the levels or effects of lapatinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 22. Lopinavir increases the levels or effects of larotrectinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. If coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors is unavoidable, reduce the larotrectinib dose by 50%. Resume the prior larotrectinib dose once the CYP3A4 inhibitor is discontinued for 3–5 half-lives. 23. Lopinavir increases the levels or effects of lefamulin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration of lefamulin with strong CYP3A inhibitors. 24. Lopinavir increases the levels or effects of lemborexant by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration of lemborexant with moderate or strong CYP3A inhibitors. 25. Lopinavir increases the levels or effects of leniolisib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 26. Lopinavir may alter estrogen plasma levels when coadministered with oral contraceptives containing levonorgestrel, ethinyl estradiol, or ferrous bisglycinate. This may reduce the efficacy of hormonal contraceptives. Use of a nonhormonal contraceptive is recommended. 27. Both lithium and lopinavir prolong the QTc interval. Avoid their concomitant use or consider alternative medications. 28. Lopinavir increases the levels or effects of lorlatinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. If unavoidable, reduce the lorlatinib dose by 25 mg/day. After discontinuing the strong CYP3A inhibitor for 3 plasma half-lives, increase to the previous lorlatinib dose. 29. Lopinavir increases the levels or effects of lurasidone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 30. Lopinavir increases the levels or effects of lurbinectedin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. If coadministration is unavoidable, reduce the lurbinectedin dose by 50%. After discontinuing the strong CYP3A inhibitor for 5 half-lives, increase lurbinectedin to the dose used before coadministration. 31. Both macimorelin and lopinavir prolong the QTc interval. Avoid their concomitant use or consider alternative medications. Macimorelin increases the corrected QT interval by approximately 11 ms. Avoid coadministration with drugs that prolong the QT interval, as this could increase the risk of torsades de pointes-type ventricular tachycardia. 32. Lopinavir increases the levels or effects of macitentan by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 33. Lopinavir increases the levels or effects of mefloquine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. Mefloquine may enhance the QTc-prolonging effect of high-risk QTc-prolonging agents. 34. Lopinavir increases the levels or effects of mestranol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 35. Lopinavir increases the levels or effects of metaxalone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 36. Lopinavir increases the levels or effects of methadone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 37. Lopinavir increases the levels or effects of methylprednisolone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 38. Lopinavir increases the levels or effects of midazolam by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs.
